clue.text: Suggestion of whip in party game?

definitions.text: Suggestion of whip in party game?

parts.words: Suggestion of whip in party game?
parts.note: a party whip's message to MPs is to vote as the leadership says, which is also the name of a children's game of copying whoever is in front

explanation.surface: A guess at how a whip might feature in some party game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests a birthday party, but the whip here is a political party's whip, the official who makes MPs vote with their leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's game in which everyone copies the person in front doubles as a whip's instruction to loyal MPs.

clue.text: It could be rude!

parts.note: read as a sly remark: the word 'rude' itself has exactly four letters, as do most swear words

explanation.surface: A warning that something might give offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to describe an obscene word, but it also works literally, since 'rude' is spelt with four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is commonly called by this name because so many English obscenities are four letters long.

clue.text: Criminal framing wife in fix gets bird

indicators.note: framing means the criminal's letters go round the rest like a picture frame

parts.note: a lag is an old slang word for a convict

indicators.note: in means the wife's letter is placed inside the word for fix

parts.note: to fix something in place is to pin it

explanation.surface: A crook who has set up his wife and landed in trouble ends up with a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a fix' reads as a phrase for trouble, but 'in' and 'fix' have separate jobs: 'in' places the wife inside the fix, and 'framing' wraps the criminal round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: The lapwing is a plover of farmland and marshes, also called the peewit, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: As some boats flew, seconds lost

indicators.note: lost tells us the letter for seconds is dropped from the word for flew

parts.note: to fly high is to soar, so flew gives soared

explanation.surface: Some boats flew across the water, losing a few seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the S from SOARED leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing boats are propelled by oars, so a boat fitted with them is described with this adjective.

clue.text: American swimmer's low fins switching height

parts.note: to low is to make a cow's sound, to moo

indicators.note: switching means the letters of fins and the H are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An American fish has low-set fins that change position as it swims up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective describing the fins, but it is the cow's verb; 'switching' shuffles the fins together with the height letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The moonfish is a name for several fish of American waters, so it is a kind of swimmer from that region.

clue.text: One done in spring

parts.note: done means fooled, and the first of a spring month is the day for tricking people

explanation.surface: Something that gets carried out during the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Done' looks like 'carried out', but in slang to be done is to be tricked, as people are on the first day of April.
explanation.definitionFit: The person tricked by a prank on the first of April is so called, and that day falls in spring.

clue.text: Literary taste but about right

indicators.note: about means the word for but goes around the letter for right

parts.note: but, as in all but one, means except

explanation.surface: A remark that someone has literary taste but is not quite correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary taste' sounds like refined judgement in books, but here a taste is a small sample.
explanation.definitionFit: A short passage taken from a book gives a reader a sample, a taste, of the whole work.

clue.text: Once mistaken about island, personality theorist left area with bleak outlook

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes round the following pieces
mistaken means the letters of once are put in the wrong order

parts.note: Crete is the large Greek island
Carl Jung was the Swiss psychologist who theorised introvert and extravert personality types

explanation.surface: A psychologist who once got things wrong about an island left for a grim place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistaken' rearranges 'Once', and 'about' splits that anagram so its last letter closes the word after the island, theorist and left are inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a grim built-up city district of grey buildings, so it is an area with a dreary outlook.

clue.text: Top university job filled by combination of results

indicators.note: filled by means the word for job has the combination placed inside it

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a perm, short for permutation, is a combination of match results on a football pools coupon

explanation.surface: A top university post goes to whoever gets the right mix of results.
explanation.walkthrough: On British football pools, betting on whether matches end in draws, a perm is a set of combinations of results; 'filled by' places it after the job's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppermost is an adjective meaning highest or on top.

clue.text: Clergyman curtailed side

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having its tail cut, so the last letter of the clergyman goes

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest in the Church of England

explanation.surface: A clergyman cut short, whose side is put across briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the final R from RECTOR leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand side of an open book, the front of a printed leaf.

clue.text: Thin character hugged by fat, rich Scotsman

indicators.note: hugged by means the thin letter is held inside the word for fat

parts.note: lard is cooking fat from pigs
I is the thinnest-looking letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A slender figure is embraced by a fat, wealthy Scot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin character' looks like a slim person but is the letter I, a narrow upright stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a landed estate, so a wealthy Scottish landowner.

clue.text: As legend would have it, models lick floor

indicators.note: models as a verb means shapes, so the letters of lick floor are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fashion models getting down to lick the floor, the stuff of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Models' reads as fashion models, but it is a verb, shaping the letters of LICK FLOOR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Folkloric means belonging to folklore, the traditional tales and legends of a people.

clue.text: Most mean to remove opener from contest in cricket match

indicators.note: in means the shortened contest goes inside the cricket match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, so the contest loses its first letter

parts.note: a fight is a contest

explanation.surface: The stingiest way to win is to take the openers out of the contest in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opener' suggests a cricket opening batsman, but it means the first letter of the contest; 'in' then places the remainder inside the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight means stingy with money, so the superlative means the most miserly.

clue.text: Lens takes little animal from big, in toto

indicators.note: in means the shortened beast goes inside the word toto

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: takes means the little animal is subtracted from the big one

parts.note: big here stands for a big animal, the elephant
an ant is a tiny insect

explanation.surface: A camera lens captures a small animal and a big one, all of it at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' stands for a big beast here; 'takes' subtracts the little animal from it, and 'in' sets what remains after the first letter of toto.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephoto is a camera lens that magnifies distant subjects, so it is a type of lens.

clue.text: The spirit of Nebuchadnezzar?

parts.note: spirit as in courage is British slang for nerve, and a nebuchadnezzar is a giant wine container holding twenty ordinary ones

explanation.surface: A question about the soul of the Babylonian king.
explanation.walkthrough: Nebuchadnezzar looks like the Babylonian king, but it is also the name of a huge champagne container; 'bottle' is also British slang for courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebuchadnezzar is an oversized wine vessel, and in British slang the same word means nerve or courage.

clue.text: Leaves having no function inside trunk?

definitions.meaning: the leaves of a book are its pages, and extra pages at the back form this section
a small pouch of gut in the body with no known use

explanation.surface: Foliage that serves no purpose inside a tree's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' and 'trunk' suggest a tree, but they mean a book's pages and the human torso.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a section of supplementary pages at the end of a book and a useless organ inside the body.

clue.text: Male with weak back needs injection of boron to preserve body

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the boron letter goes into the reversed pieces
back means the letters of male and weak together are read backwards

parts.note: lame means weak or feeble, as in a lame excuse
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: A man with a bad back needs a boron injection to keep his body going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses M plus LAME to give EMALM, and 'needs injection of' puts B into it. 'Weak back' reads as a sore back, but 'back' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To embalm a corpse is to treat it with preservatives to keep it from decaying.

clue.text: An orderly order?

parts.note: the phrase for perfect neatness pairs this pudding with the word order, so a neat arrangement is that kind of order

explanation.surface: A question about a well-arranged request.
explanation.walkthrough: In English, 'in apple-pie order' means perfectly neat; the clue asks for the word that describes such an orderly order.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for perfect tidiness uses this pudding's name as its qualifier, so it describes a very orderly order.

clue.text: Quite a serious problem's contained

indicators.note: 's stands for has, so the problem has the answer held inside the words before it

explanation.surface: A remark that something is quite a serious problem.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside 'quiTE A SERious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a puzzle or tricky question, so it is a kind of problem to solve.

clue.text: Thousand trapped by ludicrous price in trouble, subject to process

indicators.note: in means the combination goes inside the word for trouble

parts.note: woe is misery or trouble

indicators.note: trapped by means the thousand letter is held within the rearranged price
ludicrous means the letters of price become absurd, jumbled

explanation.surface: A ridiculous price leaves a thousand stuck in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ludicrous' rearranges the price, 'trapped by' holds the thousand letter inside that anagram after its first letter, and 'in' sets the lot inside the word for trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A workpiece is an object being worked on by a tool or machine, something undergoing a manufacturing process.

clue.text: Yank no good after exile in African languages

indicators.note: after means the shortened yank comes after the word for exile

parts.note: to ban someone can mean to banish or exile them

indicators.note: G stands for good, and no good means that letter is removed

parts.note: to yank is to pull sharply, to tug

explanation.surface: An American who is no good is sent into exile among African peoples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a verb here; 'no good' strips the G for good from it, and 'after' puts it behind the word for exile.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantu is the name of a large family of related languages spoken across central and southern Africa.

clue.text: Return of sailor I love figures in relationship.

indicators.note: return means the word for sailor comes back, read backwards

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sailor comes home and says I love the figures in our relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' reads the sailor backwards; love as O comes from the tennis score for zero.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation between two quantities, expressed in figures such as three to one.

clue.text: Tragic design, and disastrous

indicators.note: disastrous means the letters of design and are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tragic design, and a disastrous one at that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disastrous' rearranges DESIGN AND into the answer. It reads as a word describing the design, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something saddening causes sorrow, much as a tragic event does.

clue.text: Destination for victims of cabinet reshuffle? (6,8) 22,880

definitions.text: Destination for victims of cabinet reshuffle?

parts.words: Destination for victims of cabinet reshuffle?
parts.note: ministers sacked in a reshuffle of the governing party are out of work, so they would head to the old office for job seekers, with a pun on the party's name

explanation.surface: Where sacked ministers end up after a government shake-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The old British government job centre's name doubles as a swap of Labour Party ministers, which is what a cabinet reshuffle is.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former name of the British state office where unemployed people looked for work and claimed benefit.
